To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular specificities of R factor-determined β-lactam-ases can be classified into two types and that the molecular specificity of each β-lactam is correlated with the compatibility group of the R factor that determines it.
the R factors of compatibility group FII, I, N, C and O determined β-lactam resistance by the TEM-1 type of β-lacta- mase.

R factor-determined β-lactam-ases could be classified into two types, one of which was determined by a large group of R factors and was characterized by a uniform substrate specificity, while the other type was determined by a smaller group of R factors with a heterogeneous substrate specificity, but with all members of the group having the ability to hydro-lyze oxacillins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular specificities of the β-lactam hydrolyzing enzymes determined by 29 plasmids.
the molecular specificities of β-lacta-mases determined by 27 ampicillin resistance R factors.
the molecular properties of β-lacta-mases determined by R factors and their correlation with the compatibility of the R factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the R factor compatibility group is not a good criterion for predicting the substrate specificity of the β-lactam-ase.
R factors of the FI compatibility group determine β-lactam-ases which hydrolyze ampicillin, cephalothin, cefazolin, and cefoxitin but not oxacillin.
the β-lactam resistance of the plasmid-determined ampicillin resistance R factors is due to the TEM-type of β-lacta-mase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all the R factors tested could be divided into four compatibility groups (FII, FI, Iα and Iε) and that the β-lactam resistance pattern was correlated with the R factor compatibility group.

R factor-determined β-lactam-ases are not uniform in substrate specificity and that the TEM-type β-lac-tamases are determined by R factors belonging to the same compatibility groups as the R factors determining the TEM-type enzymes.

the TEM-type β-lac-tamases were determined exclusively by plasmids of compatibility group FII and its derivatives, and that oxacillin-hydro-lyzing β-lac-tamas were determined by plasmids not belonging to this group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular specificity of β-lacta-mase is not related to the molecular weight of the enzyme, but is related to its origin.
there is no correlation between plasmid compatibility and β-lactam specificity, and that the TEM-type β-l lactamase is determined by many different plasmids.
R factors are a heterogeneous collection of genetic elements that can be divided into two groups based on molecular specificity.
